mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat every capitalized token as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character, to avoid accidental merging of distinct persons.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a new name appears in the narrative.
mathgap.example: Treating "Alicia" and "Alicia" as the same variable leads to incorrect equations.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: Interpret "the difference between the number of X that A and B have" as the signed subtraction A - B, preserving the order of the names as written.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses the phrase "difference between".
mathgap.example: Reading "the difference between Alice and Bob" as |Alice - Bob| instead of Alice - Bob loses sign information.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement "X has N items" appears, assign X = N at that point, overwriting any previous value for X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count statement is encountered.
mathgap.example: Failing to overwrite a previous count for X and keeping the old value leads to inconsistent totals.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application (Bidirectional)
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer "X gives K items to Y" immediately when it appears, subtracting K from X and adding K to Y, using the current counts at that moment.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer statement is read.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer before an earlier one changes the amounts that are transferred.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: As soon as a variable’s exact numeric value is known, replace that variable with its value in all later equations and statements, propagating the information forward.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a variable’s value becomes determined.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known value as a symbolic variable in later equations prevents solving the system.

mathgap.title: Chronological Comparative Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement compares two persons using "more" or "fewer", translate it into a signed equation A - B = K (or ‑K) and evaluate it using the current counts at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a comparative statement of the form "A has K more/fewer than B" appears.
mathgap.example: A has 5 more oranges than B, but the solver incorrectly sets A = B ‑ 5.

mathgap.title: Signed Difference Equality Handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two signed differences, keep the subtraction order on each side exactly as written and evaluate the equality using the current counts, updating variables accordingly.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence of the form "The number of X that A has more than B equals the difference between the number of Y that C and D have" is encountered.
mathgap.example: Treating the equality as |A - B| = |C - D| instead of preserving sign loses information.

mathgap.title: Equal Distribution Operations
mathgap.principle: For "A and B redistribute ..." combine A and B’s current counts, divide the total by two, and assign each that result, overriding previous values. For "A splits all the cucumbers she owns equally among B and C", give half of A’s current count to each B and C and set A’s count to zero.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a redistribution or split‑equally statement appears.
mathgap.example: C splits all the oranges she owns equally among D and E, but the solver incorrectly gives each of D and E (C + D)/2 oranges and leaves C unchanged.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer Handling
mathgap.principle: When a conditional transfer appears ("If X has more than K items, X will transfer their items to Y"), evaluate X’s current count at that point; if the condition holds, move all of X’s items to Y (X becomes 0, Y gains the amount).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a conditional transfer statement is read.
mathgap.example: If F has more than 10 oranges, F will transfer their oranges to G, but the solver transfers regardless of F’s count.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative Increase Handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "The number of X that Y has increases by p/q times", compute the new count as Y_new = Y_current × (1 + p/q) and replace Y’s count with this value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When an increase‑by‑fraction statement is encountered.
mathgap.example: H's oranges increase by 3/2 times, but the solver incorrectly sets H_new = H_old × 3/2 instead of H_old × 5/2.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often confuses the order of subtraction, turning A - B = K into B - A = K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always write the equation as A - B = K for "A has K more than B" and double‑check the sign.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops sign information, interpreting "difference" as a magnitude.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the subtraction order and keep the sign when translating difference statements.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies later transfers before earlier ones, mixing up the amounts moved.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfer statements exactly in the order they appear, using the current counts each time.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model adds the original holder’s count to the recipients or leaves the original with half, instead of giving away all.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When "X splits all the cucumbers she owns equally among Y and Z" appears, give X/2 to Y, X/2 to Z, and set X = 0.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model either ignores the condition or transfers only part of the amount.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Check the condition using X’s current count; if true, move the entire amount from X to the target, making X = 0.
